moved.sentence: **Delegation defines interface boundaries.** A component with a clean delegate protocol is designed to be replaceable — the delegate protocol IS the interface.

judged.note: should-scope-component-with-its-delegate-protocol keeps 'delegation defines interface boundaries'; the rationale keeps the designed-to-be-replaceable and protocol-is-the-interface reason.

moved.sentence: The component and its protocol belong in the same scope group; its concrete delegate implementations may belong elsewhere.

judged.note: The two rules keep component-and-protocol in one scope group (unkeyed, now SHOULD) and concrete delegate implementations possibly elsewhere (MAY).

moved.sentence: **Notification center usage is an implicit coupling signal.** For every `NotificationCenter.post`, identify all files that observe that notification — they are implicitly coupled even if they have no import relationship.

judged.note: should-identify-notification-observers keeps identifying every observer of each NotificationCenter.post as an implicit coupling signal; the rationale keeps the coupled-without-import-relationship reason.

moved.sentence: **Singletons couple everything to everything.** Any file that accesses a singleton is implicitly coupled to every other file that accesses the same singleton.

judged.note: should-flag-cross-group-singletons keeps 'singletons couple everything to everything' and the rationale keeps that every accessor is coupled to every other accessor of the same singleton.

moved.sentence: Singletons accessed across many candidate groups indicate a cross-cutting dependency — flag for `cross-cutting-detection`.

judged.note: should-flag-cross-group-singletons keeps that cross-group singletons indicate a cross-cutting dependency and must be flagged for cross-cutting-detection, at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **DI containers define the composition boundary.** The DI container registration site is the architectural seam — it is where modules are wired together.

judged.note: should-split-scope-groups-at-di-registration keeps 'DI containers define the composition boundary'; the rationale keeps the registration site as the seam where modules are wired.

moved.sentence: Code on either side of the registration site belongs in separate scope groups.

judged.note: should-split-scope-groups-at-di-registration keeps code on either side of the registration site in separate scope groups, at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **Coordinators are natural scope group boundaries.** A coordinator object that manages navigation for a feature flow — and owns the child view controllers in that flow — is a natural scope group boundary.

judged.note: should-group-coordinator-with-owned-screens keeps the coordinator managing a feature flow and owning its child view controllers as a natural scope group boundary.

moved.sentence: The coordinator and its owned screens form one group.

judged.note: should-group-coordinator-with-owned-screens keeps that the coordinator and its owned screens form one group, at SHOULD.

moved.sentence: **Global state (Redux, MobX, Context) makes boundaries fuzzy.** If all components read from a single global store, module boundaries are implicitly bypassed.

judged.note: The rationale keeps both sentences: global state makes boundaries fuzzy and a single global store bypasses module boundaries; the rule scopes the action to Redux/MobX/Context.

moved.sentence: Document which store slices each candidate group reads/writes — slices may suggest sub-boundaries.

judged.note: should-document-store-slices-per-group keeps documenting the store slices each group reads/writes and that slices may suggest sub-boundaries.
